description: Large cave system with evidence of Romano-British activity from the late 1st to the early 4th CE. Cautiously interpreted as a religious site, but with the presence of craft working a dual nature had been proposed, some authors have gone so far as to connect the site with Mithraism. The RSRB marks the site as a 'shrine'.
bibliography: Allen, Martyn, Tom Brindle, Alex Smith, Julian D Richards, Tim Evans, Neil Holbrook, Michael Fulford, and Nathan Blick. “The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: An Online Resource.” Archaeology Data Service, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
Dearne, Martin J., and Thomas C. Lord. The Romano-British Archaeology of Victoria Cave, Settle: Researches into the Site and Its Artefacts. BAR 273. Oxford: Archaeopress Hadrian books, 1998.
